memoryText: You shall call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Matthew 1:21 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
An angel speaks these words to Joseph in a dream, and they contain the whole mission of Jesus in one sentence.

“You shall call his name Jesus.” The name is the Greek form of Joshua, which means “the LORD saves.” Names in Scripture often carry meaning, and this one is a sermon. Joseph does not choose it. God does. Joseph is asked to take the child as his own and to give him the name.

“For he will save.” The verb is about rescue. Matthew does not say he will try, or offer help, or point the way. He will save. The child in the manger is the rescuer.

“His people.” The people are those who belong to him. In the Old Testament, that meant Israel. By the end of this Gospel, it includes people from every nation who follow him. Matthew begins with a family tree that includes outsiders for a reason.

“From their sins.” This is the surprising part. A first-century Jew would have expected rescue from Rome. Matthew says the deepest problem is not political but moral, and the solution is a Savior who deals with sin itself. He does this at the cross, where he bears it.

Say this verse whenever you wonder what Jesus came to do. He came to save his people from their sins, and that includes you if you belong to him.
weekInReview: This week you finished the Old Testament and began the New. You read Zechariah’s vision of a fountain, a pierced one, and the LORD as king over all the earth. In Malachi you heard God’s love, his rebuke, and the promise of a messenger and a sun of righteousness. You reviewed the whole Unit 14 story of the return. Then, on the first two days of Matthew, you saw the genealogy that gathers up the covenants of Abraham and David, the virgin birth and the name Jesus, the Magi who came to worship, and the escape to Egypt. You watched John prepare the way, Jesus baptized with the Father’s voice from heaven, and Jesus overcome the devil’s temptations by quoting Deuteronomy. The silence between the Testaments is over, and the promises are arriving in a person.
reflectionQuestions: Matthew’s genealogy includes Tamar, Rahab, and Ruth. What does that tell you about the kind of people Jesus came for?
The name Jesus means “the LORD saves.” In what area of your life do you most need to remember that he saves?
Jesus answered each temptation with Scripture. Which Scripture is helping you stand right now, and which one might you memorize next?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for coming to save his people from their sins.
Thank God for the long story that led to him.
